newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi chairman plans to quit JSDA head--Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi chairman plans to quit JSDA head--Kyodo.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd chairman Tsugio Yukihira intends to resign the chairmanship of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) following a raid on Yamaichi's offices on Wednesday, Kyodo news agency reported.
A Yamaichi spokesman said he could not immediately confirm the report.
Earlier on Wednesday, officials of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission and prosecutors raided the brokerage for alleged violations of Japanese securities laws.
Prosecutors said they suspected Yamaichi, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, paid 79 million yen to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, Ryuichi Koike.

Yukihira became acting chairman of the JSDA after Nomura Securities Co Ltd chairman Masashi Suzuki resigned after Nomura's involvement in an illegal payoff scandal involving the same sokaiya surfaced in March.
Kyodo said an official announcement of the resignation was expected within a few days.
